questions.q_en: A civil contractor planned to build an over bridge of 3 km distance in 600 days. For this purpose, he employed 90 workers. After 200 days of work, it was observed that only 0.5 km of the bridge was completed. What is the number of extra workers required to complete the work in time?
questions.solution_en:
Remaining work = 3 - 0.5 = 2.5

Remaining days = 600 - 200 = 400

Let the number of extra workers required = m

According to the question-

m + 90 =

m + 90 = 225

m = 225 - 90

m = 135

questions.q_en: If 6 women can complete a work in 3 days, and 9 girls can complete the same work in 2 days, then find the time taken to complete the same work by 8 women and 6 girls?
questions.solution_en:
Work done by 6 women in 1 day = 1/3

So, work done by 8 women in 1 day = 8/(3 * 6) = 4/9

And work done by 9 girls in 1 day = ½

And work done by 6 girls in 1 day = 6/(2 * 9) = 1/3

So, work done by 8 women and 6 girls together in 1 day = 4/9 + 1/3 = 7/9

So, required time = 9/7 days

questions.q_en: 18 workers can complete a piece of work in 96 days. They start working together and after 26 days 10 more workers join them. In how many days in all will the work be completed?
questions.solution_en:
Total work = 18 * 96 = 1728 worker-days

Work done in 26 days by 18 workers = 18 * 26 = 468 worker-days

Remaining work = 1728 - 468 = 1260 worker-days

Days for remaining work = 1260/(18 + 10) = 45 days

Total days = 26 + 45 = 71 days

questions.q_en: A is 20% more efficient than B. How much time will they working together take to complete a job which A alone could have done in 29 days?
questions.solution_en:
A alone can complete the whole work in = 29 days

So, B alone can complete the whole work in = 29 * 120/100 = 174/5 days

Hence, both of them together can complete the whole work = 1/(1/29 + 5/174) = 174/11 days

questions.q_en: A can complete a certain work in 35 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They worked together for 7 days, then B left the work. In how many days will A alone complete 60% of the remaining work?
questions.solution_en:
Let total work = LCM of 35 and 15 = 105 units

Part of work done by A in 1 day = 105/35 = 3 units

Part of work done by B in 1 day = 105/15 = 7 units

Total work done by A and B together in 7 days = 7 * (3 + 7) = 70 units

Remaining work = 105 - 70 = 35 units

Time taken by A alone to complete 60% of remaining work = (60% of 35)/3

= 7 days

questions.q_en: Ravi and Sanju together can do a job in 2 days, Sanju and Mahesh can do it in 4 days, while Ravi and Mahesh can do it in 2 days. What is the number of days required for Ravi to do the same job alone?
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 2, 4 and 2 = 4 units

Efficiency of Ravi + Sanju = 4/2 = 2 ----(1)

Efficiency of Mahesh + Sanju = 4/4 = 1 ----(2)

Efficiency of Ravi + Mahesh = 4/2 = 2 ------(3)

eqn (1) + eqn(3) - eqn(2):

2 * Efficiency of Ravi = 2 + 2 - 1 = 3

Efficiency of Ravi = 3/2

Time taken by Ravi = 4/(3/2) = 8/3 days

questions.q_en: 6 men and 8 women can do a piece of work in 10 days, whereas 26 man and 48 women can so the same work in 2 days. What will be the time taken by 15 men and 20 women to do the same work?
questions.solution_en:
Let work done by 1 man in 1 day = m and work done by 1 woman in 1 day = b

Work done by 6 men and 8 women in 1 day = 1/10

=> 6m + 8b = 1/10

=> 60m + 80b = 1 ---(1)

Work done by 26 men and 48 women in 1 day = 1/2

=> 26m + 48b =1/2

=> 52m + 96b = 1 ---(2)

Solving equation 1 and equation 2. We get m = 1/100 and b = 1/200

Work done by 15 men and 20 women in 1 day.

= 15/100 + 20/200 =1/4

=> Time taken by 15 men and 20 women in doing the work = 4 days

questions.q_en: A and B can do a work in 13 days and 26 days, respectively. If they work for a day alternately, starting with A, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 13 and 26 = 26

Efficiency of A = 26/13 = 2

Efficiency of B = 26/26 = 1

Total work in 16 days = 8(2+1) = 24 units

Work on 9th day by A = 2 units

Total time = 16 + 1 = 17 days

questions.q_en: Ten men begin to do a work. But after some days, four of them left the job. As a result, the job that could have been completed in 40 days is completed in 50 days. How many days after the commencement of the work did the four men leave?
questions.solution_en:
Let the number of days after which 4 men leave the job = d

According to the question-

10 (40 - d) = 6 (50-d)

400 - 10d = 300 - 6d

4d = 100

d = 25 days

questions.q_en: A group of men decided to do a job in 6 days, but 18 men dropped out every day. If the job was completed in 8 days, then how many men initially decided to do the job?
questions.solution_en:
Let the initial number of men = a

Total work = 6a

a + (a - 18) + (a - 36) ...... 8 terms = 6a

8a - (18 + 36 + 54 + ...7 terms) = 6a

2a = [2*18 + (7-1) * 18]

2a = [36 + 108]

a = * 144

a = 252

Hence, the initial number of men = 252

questions.q_en: Tarun is twice as good as Tripti in doing a work. Together, they can complete the work in 16 days. In how many days can Tripti alone complete the same work?
questions.solution_en:
Efficiency of Tarun and Tripti = 2:1

Total work = (2 + 1)*16 = 48 units

Time taken by Tripti alone = 48/1 = 48 days

questions.q_en: A and B together can complete a certain work in 20 days whereas B and C together can complete it in 24 days. If A is twice as good a work man as C, then in what time will B alone do 40% of the same work?
questions.solution_en:
A = 2C

LCM of 20 and 24 = 120

Efficiency of A and B = 120/20 = 6

Efficiency of B and C = 120/24 = 5

2C + B = 6 ------(1)

B + C = 5 -------(2)

Subtracting eq(2) from eq(1) -

C = 1, B = 4

Time taken by B to complete 40% of total work = 120* (40/100) * (1/4) = 12 days

questions.q_en: 5 men and 8 women can complete a work in 12 days working together, while 3 men and 7 women together can complete the same work in 15 days. In how many days will 11 women complete the same work?
questions.solution_en:
Let work done by 1 man in a day = m

Work done by 1 woman in a day = w

So,

5m + 8w = 1/12→ 15m + 24w = ¼ ------------(1)

3m + 7w = 1/15 → 15m + 35w = 1/3 ----------(2)

On solving both equations-

11w =1/12

So, 11 women will complete the same work in 12 days.

questions.q_en: Manish, Nakul and Pintoo alone can complete a certain work in 21 days, 28 days and 15 days, respectively. Manish and Pintoo started the work together while Nakul joined them after 5 days and worked with them till the completion of the work. For how many days did Nakul work?
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 21, 28 and 15 = 420 units

Efficiency of Manish = 420/21 = 20

Efficiency of Nakul = 420/28 = 15

Efficiency of Pintoo = 420/15 = 28

Work done by Manish and Pintoo in 5 days = 5(20 + 28) = 240 units

Remaining work = 420 - 240 = 180 units

Time taken by all three persons to complete remaining work = 180/(20 + 15 + 28) = 20/7 = 2(6/7) days

Hence, Nakul did the work for 2(6/7) days.

questions.q_en: A can complete 25% of a work in 15 days. He works for 15 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 30 days. In how many days will A and B working together finish 50% of the same work?
questions.solution_en:
Time in which A alone can complete the whole work = 15 * 100/25 = 60 days

15 days' work done by A alone = 15/60 = 1/4

Remaining work = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4

Now, time in which B alone can complete the whole work = 30 * 4/3 = 40 days

Therefore, time taken by A and B together to finish 50% of the work

= 50/100 * 1/(1/60 + 1/40)

= 12 days

questions.q_en: A can complete a piece of work alone in 200 days, while B can complete the same piece of work alone in 100 days. In every three-day cycle, both A and B work on day 1, only A works on day 2, and only B works on day 3. This cycle continues till the work is completed. How many days in all does it take the duo to complete the work?
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 200 and 100 = 200 units

Efficiency of A = 200/200 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 200/100 = 2 units/day

Total work in 3 days = (1 + 2) + 1 + 2 = 6 units

Total work in 99 days = 33 * 6 = 198 units

Remaining = 200 - 198 = 2 units

Total = 99 + 2/3 = 99(2/3) days

questions.q_en: Eighteen persons working 8 hours a day can complete 3 units of work in 10 days. How many days are required by 25 persons to complete 5 units of work working 6 hours a day?
questions.solution_en:
Since total work = Persons * days * hours/Unit of works

(18*8*10)/3=(25*d*6)/5

480 = 30d

d = 16 days

questions.q_en: Ronak and Riya can do a work in 12 and 18 days, respectively. They worked together for six days and then Ronak left. Find the time taken by Riya to complete the work.
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units

Efficiency of Ronak = 36/12 = 3

Work done by Ronak and Riya in 6 days = 6(3 + 2) = 30 units

Remaining work = 36 - 30 = 6 units

Time taken by Riya to complete remaining work = 6/2 = 3 days

questions.q_en: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 25 days, B and C together can complete the same piece of work in 36 days, while C and A together can complete it in 30 days. If A, B, C, and D together can complete this piece of work in 18 days, then in how many days can D alone complete this piece of work?
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 25, 36, 30 and 18 = 900 units

Efficiency of A + B = 900/25 = 36 ----(1)

Efficiency of B + C = 900/36 = 25 ----(2)

Efficiency of C + A = 900/30 = 30 ------(3)

Efficiency of A + B + C + D = 900/18 = 50 ------(4)

Eqn(4) - [eqn (1) + eqn(2) + eqn(3)]/2:

Efficiency of D = 50 - (36 + 25 + 30)/2 = 50 - 45.5 = 4.5

Time taken by D = 900/4.5 = 200 days

questions.q_en: P can do a piece of work in 30 days and Q in 40 days. They work together for 4 days and then Q leaves. The number of days taken by P to finish the remaining work is:
questions.solution_en:
Total work = LCM of 30 and 40 = 120 units

Efficiency of P = 120/30 = 4

Efficiency of Q = 120/40 = 3

Work done in 4 days = 4(4 + 3) = 28

Remaining work = 120 - 28 = 92 units

Time taken by P to finish the remaining work = 92/4 = 23 days
